page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with a single thread per core under a shared CPU allocation model. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.e4.xlarge exhibits constrained performance characteristics, largely due to its older processor architecture and shared CPU allocation. In stress-ng testing, single-core performance falls into the bottom 10%, while multi-core performance is in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests, including read-only large block (30.12 GB/sec) and write large block (22.11 GB/sec), also rank in the bottom 25%. These metrics suggest that while the instance offers a generous memory capacity, memory access speeds and processing throughput are limited, making it less suitable for compute-intensive workloads.

Given its high memory capacity relative to compute resources, the ecs.e4.xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-performance CPU throughput. It is suitable for hosting lightweight databases, caching layers, or general-purpose applications with moderate traffic where memory footprint is a priority over raw processing speed. However, workloads requiring high-speed cryptography, intensive vector operations, or rapid local storage I/O should avoid this instance due to the lack of local storage and lower benchmark scores in database operations and encryption tests.
